00202.setting: Locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
00202.schedule: Docetaxel 100 mg/m² IV over 60 minutes on day 1 every 21 days.
00202.duration: Repeat until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; no universal fixed number of cycles.
ongoing: FBC, renal and liver profile before every cycle
Clinical toxicity and disease response review according to the agreed plan
00202.cardiac: No fixed cardiac imaging schedule is specified for this monotherapy.
support: Dexamethasone 8 mg orally twice daily for 3 days starting the day before infusion; at least 3 doses before treatment.
If the oral course is missed, contact the team: the consultant may consider 20 mg IV immediately before infusion. This is not an automatic extra dose.
G-CSF prophylaxis may be used according to risk and local policy.
Low emetogenic category; use local antiemetic plan.

bodymap.blood: Neutropenia, infection and possible febrile neutropenia
bodymap.fluid: Fluid retention; steroid course is important
bodymap.infusion: Severe hypersensitivity requires immediate cessation and no rechallenge
bodymap.bowel: Neutropenic enterocolitis is an urgent concern

00230.setting: Metastatic breast cancer after failure of first-line metastatic chemotherapy when standard anthracycline therapy is not indicated
00230.schedule: Nab-paclitaxel 260 mg/m² IV over 30 minutes on day 1 every 21 days.
00230.duration: Repeat until progression or unacceptable toxicity; NCCP also directs discontinuation if there is no response after 2 cycles.
baseline: Cardiac assessment if significant cardiac history or previous anthracycline exposure
ongoing: FBC, renal and liver profile before every cycle
Assess treatment response, including the source review after 2 cycles
00230.cardiac: History/exposure-triggered baseline assessment, then clinical indication; no fixed HER2-style echo schedule.
support: Premedication is not usually required.
Low emetogenic risk; antiemetics follow local policy.
Use the nab-paclitaxel formulation; do not substitute conventional paclitaxel.

bodymap.heart_lungs: Report new breathlessness, chest symptoms or cough urgently

00736.setting: Metastatic breast cancer after anthracycline failure or when anthracyclines are unsuitable; alternative when standard paclitaxel is unsuitable, including hypersensitivity
00736.schedule: Nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² IV over 30 minutes on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle; day 22 is a break.
00736.duration: Repeat while beneficial and tolerated, until progression or unacceptable toxicity; no fixed total number of cycles.
baseline: Cardiac assessment if significant cardiac history or previous anthracycline exposure
ongoing: FBC, renal and liver profile at the start of each cycle
Day 8 FBC explicitly listed by NCCP
The treating service must confirm day 15 blood-test timing and dose-day count eligibility
Assess neuropathy and other toxicity before each administration; cardiac monitoring if clinically indicated
00736.cardiac: Conditional cardiac assessment; no universal repeated echo interval.
support: This weekly schedule is off label; local consent and Drugs and Therapeutics Committee governance apply.
Premedication is not usually required; low emetogenic risk.
Use nab-paclitaxel specifically; it is not interchangeable with conventional paclitaxel.

bodymap.blood: Counts may delay a dose or the next cycle
bodymap.nerves: Neuropathy; the baseline grade-2 exclusion differs from the toxicity-table recovery wording and requires specialist review
bodymap.heart_lungs: New breathlessness, chest symptoms or cough require prompt review

00743.setting: Locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after at least one chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease; previous anthracycline and taxane unless unsuitable
00743.schedule: Eribulin 1.23 mg/m² as base (equivalent to 1.4 mg/m² mesylate) IV over 5 minutes on days 1 and 15 every 28 days.
00743.duration: Repeat until progression or unacceptable toxicity; no fixed total number of cycles.
baseline: ECG when heart failure, bradyarrhythmia, QT-prolonging medicines or electrolyte abnormalities create risk
Correct low potassium, calcium or magnesium before initiation
ongoing: NCCP: FBC, renal and liver profile at the start of every cycle
EMA Halaven SmPC section 4.4 additionally requires full blood count before each dose, including day 15
Monitor electrolytes periodically; ECG if clinically indicated
Assess peripheral neuropathy and current toxicity before each dose
00743.cardiac: QT/ECG monitoring depends on risk and symptoms; no routine HER2 echo schedule.
support: No routine premedication; low emetogenic risk.
G-CSF may be used for severe neutropenia.
Unlicensed 28-day posology: explain and consent under local policy; Drugs and Therapeutics Committee acknowledgement.
Review QT-prolonging antiemetics, including ondansetron, if predisposed.
Optional trastuzumab is a separate prescribed regimen (00200), not automatically part of this monotherapy suite.

bodymap.heart: QT prolongation, with electrolyte and medicine review
bodymap.energy: Tiredness or dizziness may affect driving

supplement.fact: Full blood count before each dose

00485.setting: Adjuvant or neoadjuvant high-risk node-negative or node-positive breast cancer
00485.schedule: AC: doxorubicin 60 mg/m² plus cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² on day 1 every 14 days for 4 cycles. Start paclitaxel 14 days after the last AC: 80 mg/m² weekly for 12 doses, recorded as days 1, 8 and 15 of four 21-day cycles.
00485.duration: Approximately 20 planned weeks including the final cycle interval, before any delays. Last planned weekly infusion is around week 19 from the first AC dose; completion/recovery review follows the individual plan.
baseline: Echo or MUGA if age >65 or clinically indicated; source requires LVEF >50% for doxorubicin
Assess peripheral neuropathy as clinically indicated
Review all previous anthracyclines and cumulative-dose risk
ongoing: FBC, renal and liver profile before each cycle
The service confirms blood-test timing before weekly doses
Cardiac testing (MUGA/echo/ECG) and neuropathy assessment as clinically indicated
Confirm the phase before using count, liver or supportive-care rules
00485.cardiac: Anthracycline exposure and clinical risk guide monitoring. No trastuzumab is in this regimen and no routine HER2 q12-week echo schedule applies.
support: G-CSF is required with every dose-dense AC cycle; type and timing follow the prescribed local plan.
G-CSF is not automatically mandatory throughout weekly paclitaxel; consider it for the specified severe/prolonged neutropenia or other clinical risk.
AC is highly emetogenic; weekly paclitaxel is low. Keep the two antiemetic plans separate.
Paclitaxel first dose: dexamethasone 8 mg IV, chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV, each 30 minutes before.

From day 8: no routine dexamethasone; chlorphenamine 10 mg IV and famotidine 20 mg IV continue. Consultant may add dexamethasone for increased risk/previous reaction or omit famotidine if no reaction; monitor closely.
NCCP suggests 2–3 litres oral fluid on AC day 1 for cyclophosphamide, but the team must individualise this for cardiac/renal fluid restriction.
Analgesic cover may help paclitaxel muscle/joint aches.

bodymap.blood: Myelosuppression and infection in both phases; dose-dense AC needs G-CSF
bodymap.heart: Doxorubicin cumulative cardiac toxicity; review prior anthracyclines
